details: Iran's Revolutionary Guards reportedly fired at least two missiles at commercial ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night (July 6, 2026). This incident, which caused significant damage to two commercial vessels, marks a renewed escalation of geopolitical tensions in a critical global oil shipping lane. The attacks followed a period of indirect US-Iran talks that concluded without notable progress on maritime security, raising concerns about stability in the region and potentially increasing risk aversion in financial markets.
title: Iran Fires Missiles Near Strait of Hormuz, Escalating Tensions

details: After a prolonged period of outflows, U.S.-listed spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded net inflows of approximately $266 million on July 6, 2026. BlackRock's IBIT led these inflows with roughly $209 million, marking the second consecutive day of positive flows. This development signals a potential resurgence in institutional demand for Bitcoin following recent market volatility.
title: BlackRock's IBIT Leads $266M Inflow into US Spot Bitcoin ETFs

details: Weaker-than-expected US jobs data for June 2026, showing only 57,000 new nonfarm jobs, has led to a significant reduction in market expectations for further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. This softening labor market outlook has contributed to a weaker US dollar and a more accommodative stance from the Fed, which typically improves sentiment for risk assets, including Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies.
title: Weak US Jobs Report Lowers Rate Hike Bets, Lifting Bitcoin
